neighbours.label: 'much' in '(for) much longer' about how much longer something will continue or last, as against 'much' with other comparatives (much bigger, much more)
fire: The old bridge cannot carry heavy lorries for much longer.
I am not sure the team can keep up this pace much longer.
Doctors warned that the patient might not survive much longer without a transplant.
The shop will not stay open much longer if sales keep falling.
We could not wait much longer, so we left without him.
Experts doubt the ceasefire will hold for much longer.
The battery in my phone does not last much longer than a day.
If prices keep rising, families cannot afford this for much longer.
quiet: The new bridge can carry much heavier lorries than the old one.
The team played much better in the second half.
Doctors said the patient was much stronger after the transplant.
The shop is much busier on Saturdays than on weekdays.
We had much more fun than we expected at the fair.
Experts say the ceasefire is much more fragile than it looks.
My new phone is much faster than the old one.
Prices in the city are much higher than in the countryside.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.8 on 'much' before 'longer'; 'much' before other comparatives below 0.1
notes: Predicts 'longer' (the + pole suppresses ' much', ' significantly', so the - pole promotes them).
